# Bug Report Quality Guidelines

A checklist and reference for writing high-quality, actionable bug reports.
Every bug report generated by the jira-bug-creator skill must meet these standards.

---

## The Golden Rules of Bug Reporting

1. **One bug per report.** Do not bundle multiple issues into one report.
2. **Be specific, not vague.** "The button doesn't work" → "Clicking the 'Submit'
   button on the login form produces no response and no error message."
3. **Reproducible.** Anyone reading the report should be able to follow the steps
   and see the same result.
4. **Evidence-backed.** Every claim is supported by the screenshot or observable data.
5. **Actionable.** The developer reading it knows exactly what to fix and how to verify.

---

## Title Quality Checklist

A good bug title answers: **What? Where? When?**

| ❌ Bad Title | ✅ Good Title |
|---|---|
| "It's broken" | "Checkout page crashes when applying promo code SUMMER25" |
| "Login not working" | "Login fails with '500 Internal Server Error' for users with special characters in password" |
| "UI issue" | "User avatar overlaps with username text on profile page at 320px width" |
| "Slow" | "Dashboard takes 8+ seconds to load when more than 50 widgets are configured" |

**Title formula:** `[Component/Feature] — What happens — Under what condition`

---

## Steps to Reproduce Checklist

- [ ] **Numbered sequentially** — one action per step.
- [ ] **Start from a known state** — e.g., "Logged in as admin", "On the homepage".
- [ ] **Include exact data** — URLs, usernames, input values, file names.
- [ ] **Atomic steps** — each step is a single, observable action.
- [ ] **Prerequisites stated** — accounts, permissions, data, configuration needed.
- [ ] **Minimal path** — the shortest sequence that triggers the bug.
- [ ] **No assumptions** — if a step is unclear, mark it `[TO CONFIRM]`.

**Example:**
```
1. Navigate to https://example.com/login
2. Enter "testuser@example.com" in the Email field
3. Enter "P@ssword123!" in the Password field
4. Click the "Sign In" button
```

---

## Expected vs Actual Result Checklist

| Expected Result | Actual Result |
|---|---|
| Describes correct behavior | Describes observed behavior |
| Based on requirements/AC | Based on screenshot evidence |
| Specific and measurable | Specific and descriptive |
| Includes success indicators | Includes error messages verbatim |
| States what the user should see | States what the user actually sees |

---

## Severity Classification

| Severity | Definition | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **Critical** | System crash, data loss, security breach, complete feature outage | App crashes on launch, payment data exposed, database corrupted |
| **High** | Core feature broken, no workaround, blocks testing | Login fails for all users, checkout cannot complete, API returns 500 |
| **Medium** | Feature partially broken, workaround exists, non-critical path | Filter doesn't work but search does, UI misalignment on one browser |
| **Low** | Cosmetic issue, minor UI glitch, edge case | Typo in help text, icon slightly misaligned, hover state missing |

---

## Priority Classification

| Priority | Definition | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| **P1** | Must fix immediately, blocks release | Critical severity, or high severity on release day |
| **P2** | Should fix in current sprint, high user impact | High severity, or medium severity on a core user flow |
| **P3** | Nice to fix, can defer to next sprint | Medium severity with workaround, or low severity on core flow |
| **P4** | Backlog, low impact | Low severity cosmetic issues, edge cases rarely hit |

---

## Environment Details Checklist

Always capture:
- [ ] **Browser** name and version (e.g., Chrome 117.0.5938.132)
- [ ] **Operating System** and version (e.g., Windows 11 22H2, macOS 14.0)
- [ ] **Device type** (Desktop / Mobile / Tablet) and model if relevant
- [ ] **Screen resolution** (e.g., 1920×1080, 390×844)
- [ ] **Application version** or build number
- [ ] **Server environment** (QA / Staging / Production)
- [ ] **User role / account** used during testing

---

## Screenshot Best Practices

- [ ] Capture the **full screen** when possible — include URL bar, browser chrome.
- [ ] **Highlight** the problem area (red box, arrow) if the issue is subtle.
- [ ] Include **console output** if there are JavaScript errors.
- [ ] Include **network tab** if there are failed API calls.
- [ ] Capture **before and after** states if the bug involves a state change.
- [ ] Do **not** include sensitive data (passwords, PII, tokens) in screenshots.

---

## Common Pitfalls to Avoid

| Pitfall | Fix |
|---|---|
| "It doesn't work" | Describe exactly what happens — error message, blank screen, wrong data |
| Missing steps | Walk through the flow mentally; fill in every click, input, and navigation |
| No environment info | Check the screenshot for browser chrome, OS indicators, URL bar |
| Wrong severity | Justify your choice — what's the user impact? Is there a workaround? |
| Multiple bugs in one | Split into separate reports if the issues have different root causes |
| No expected result | Think: "If this worked correctly, what would the user see?" |
